comparison: Both address study cohort and design (C1-C6). OpenEval finds methodology clearly described with appropriate approvals (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers consistently critique small cohort size and heterogeneous population as limiting statistical power (UNCERTAIN). Major disagreement on adequacy of study design.

Perfect claim overlap (C7-C9, C29, C32, C56) regarding CD4+ T cell subset enrichment in non-responders. Both evaluations agree findings are valid (SUPPORTED), though peer reviewers note these are confirmatory rather than novel, describing them as 'well precedented' and adding weight to prior evidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C10, C30, C31, C33, C55) on CD8+ T cell activation in responders. Both evaluations support the findings (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers characterize results as 'not surprising and well precedented' but accept data quality and interpretation as valid contributions.

Perfect claim overlap (C11-C13, C39-C40, C63-C64) on pathway activation (STAT3, NFkB) in non-responders. Both evaluations support findings (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers explicitly state associations are 'well precedented' and act as confirmatory evidence rather than novel discoveries.

Partial overlap on predictive model claims (C14, C49, C66). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to small sample size, lack of validation, and potential overfitting. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, expressing serious concerns about generalizability and viewing high AUC as likely reflecting overfitting. Both identify same fundamental issues but peer review is more critical.

Partial overlap on univariate associations (C47, C48, C50). OpenEval groups these with predictive model claims (UNCERTAIN due to overfitting concerns). Peer reviewers separately evaluate univariate associations as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing multiple testing corrections negate signal and questioning biological take-aways after proper statistical adjustment.

Perfect claim overlap (C28, C67-C68) on metastatic lymph node sampling limitation. OpenEval finds authors appropriately acknowledge limitation with supporting evidence (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting lack of explicit reviewer commentary on this specific issue despite general concerns about generalizability.

Partial overlap on tumor analysis claims. OpenEval evaluates CNA correlation (C34-C35) as SUPPORTED with appropriate methods. Peer R6 addresses broader tumor signature analysis (C34-C38, C41-C42, C45-C46, C65) as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging interesting analysis but questioning robustness due to multiple testing issues.

Partial overlap on DEG analysis and RFX complex (C36-C38). OpenEval finds analysis well-supported with appropriate citations (SUPPORTED). Peer R6 groups these with broader tumor signature findings, rating UNCERTAIN due to multiple testing concerns affecting biological take-aways despite acknowledging extensive analysis as a strength.

Partial overlap on interferon signatures (C41-C42). OpenEval evaluates PCA-derived signatures with biological interpretation as SUPPORTED. Peer R6 includes these in broader tumor analysis rated UNCERTAIN, questioning robustness after multiple testing corrections despite acknowledging interesting cell program analysis.

Minimal overlap (C43-C44) on interferon context. OpenEval evaluates interferon signatures as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R9 addresses broader literature context including these claims, rating background statements as SUPPORTED since they represent accepted scientific context from prior work.

Partial overlap on signature validation (C45-C46). OpenEval finds testing in independent datasets appropriately supports ICI-response specificity (SUPPORTED). Peer R6 groups validation with broader tumor signature analysis, rating UNCERTAIN due to multiple testing concerns despite acknowledging the analysis quality.

Partial overlap on discussion of immune complexity (C57-C62). OpenEval finds discussion appropriately addresses context-dependence with extensive citations (SUPPORTED). Peer R9 groups these with broader literature context, rating SUPPORTED as they represent accepted background rather than novel claims requiring validation.

Substantial overlap (C15-C27, C51-C54) on literature review and background. Both evaluations rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations establishing scientific rationale. Peer reviewers acknowledge these as accepted scientific context from prior work, with Reviewer 3 noting findings are 'well precedented.'

Substantial overlap (C76-C86) on methodological details. Both evaluations support the methods (SUPPORTED). OpenEval notes explicit details following standard practices. Peer reviewers acknowledge methodology integration and high-quality annotation as main strengths, though emphasize need for better statistical approaches and external validation of results.

Partial overlap on ethical/methodological claims (C69-C75). OpenEval groups ethical approvals with cohort documentation, rating SUPPORTED. Peer R10 focuses on technical methodology (C69-C86), rating methods as SUPPORTED while noting integration quality and annotation strengths.
